The SF1000 report from yesterday: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md; fix specs: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/*-SPEC.md.

Refute this finding from the measurements and, where it names a mechanism, from the source: {
 "id": "scaleout-4cn-2",
 "claim": "q06's +44% (0.85 -> 1.22 s) is a dispatch serialization, not engine work: in all three runs three leaf senders start together and the fourth, always on the CN hosting the result fragment, starts 611-662 ms later right after the third finishes. Cause: the demo-plus carve has no SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH implementation, so the CN holds exec_plan_fragment open for the sender's whole run, and the FE Deployer's three-stage split (instance on an already-deployed worker goes to stage 2, deployed after stage 1 completes) turns that into a second wave.",
 "evidence": [
  "dp-cn4/cluster.log 'fragment run started': r0 three at 22:02:35.9615, fourth 22:02:36.6136 on 9112 (result on 9112); r1 22:02:37.2217 x3, fourth 22:02:37.8323 on 9102 (result on 9102); r2 22:02:38.4315 x3, fourth 22:02:39.0940 on 9112 (result on 9112). Baseline perf/sf1000/cn4/cluster.log q06: all four within 1 ms (13:19:52.9078-.9089), fragment elapsed 623-687 ms vs 431-606 ms in dp",
  "exec_plan_fragment RPC close time.idle max per run = 651/609/662 ms for q06, 2040 ms q01.r0, 1860 ms q03.r0 in dp-cn4 vs max 1 ms in every baseline run (agent-notes/_dispatch_skew.py rpc_idle_ms column)",
  "grep -rn ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH sirius-stacks-wt/demo-plus/experimental/starrocks/src = no hits (present in sirius-stacks-wt/perf/.../compute_node_service.rs:208,271,291); fix/capture-arm.sh:14 exported it anyway; dp-cn4 tunables line lists only fusion_mode=Leaf",
  "FE: demo-plus experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe/fe-core/.../qe/scheduler/Deployer.java createFragmentInstanceExecStates (deployedWorkerIds -> stage 2) and the stage loop deployAsync + waitForDeploymentCompletion; yesterday's report line 313 predicted the blocking-RPC form of this. Only q06 has a leaf sender fragment as direct child of the result fragment (5 fragments); q01's leaves start together (skew 0-1 ms) because the merge stage is deployed first (inference)"
 ],
 "confidence": "high",
 "impact": "The carve dropped the async sender dispatch / DrainTicket overlap the perf branch had; any single-stage plan pays a full extra sender run at N>1 CNs, and every sender RPC now blocks the FE's next deploy stage (the same mechanism delays the failing six's drains).",
 "task": "scaleout-4cn"
}

=== yesterday's report lines 305-320
**Objection (both skeptics).** "Directly caused q17 to die with only 66 GB of its own data parked" is arithmetically false: q17's F00 lineitem projection is ~120-122 GB (46 tasks x 2.65 GB; standalone `GPU_SCAN(3) n=46 in=122.25 GB`), above the 107.37 GB cap, so it fails with zero leak; the leak only moved the death from ~40 to 25 parked batches. The order-dependence risk is real but inferred: q07's own parked footprint is 79.17 GB; under the 38.16 GB leak it would need ~117 GB and would have failed had it run between q09 and q17. The cn1 timings of q10-q16 and q22.r1/r2 were taken with 31.6 / 36.6 GB of the pool occupied (the reservation-gate blocks in C3 need that leak to occur).

**Proposed (small, high confidence as hygiene).** Store `query_id` with each `ParkedOutput`; on `Err` drop only that query's slots; keep a failed-query set on the engine thread and skip its pending `Run`s (Err-time bookkeeping, since cancel arrives after the next sender already started); make `cancel_plan_fragment` drop the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeue its fragments (needs a `LocalExchange` removal by query; today removals happen only in `take_ready`, local_exchange.rs:284-308); in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm `drop_parked` the slots already in hand when translation fails.

#### B5 (confirmed, proposals corrected). Shuffle drains are serialised after the fragment finishes, and 84-88% of each drain is `export_packed` on the engine thread at ~63 GB/s

**Measured, cn4 q03.r1** (cn4/cluster.log): each lineitem sender finished at +0.610..0.684 s, then performed 3 sequential transmits of 4.82-4.89 GB, each `elapsed_ms=92-98 lease_ms=1-2 write_ms=6-8` (600-717 GB/s write), completing at +95/+190/+283 ms after finish; the next fragment on that CN (customer scan) started 0.1-0.3 ms after the last transmit on all 4 CNs. Same pattern in q03.r0/r2 and in q10.r1 (lineitem 0.145-0.159 s, customer 0.083-0.102 s), q12.r1 (0.115-0.125 s), q19.r1 (0.055-0.078 s). The Quent staging-lease probe times the pack directly: 48-52 sender-side leases per CN of ~311 MB, pack median 4.9 ms per lease = 63.5 GB/s, non-pack (lease RPC + write + transmit RPC) 0.7 ms, so pack = 84-88% of the drain for q03 (74-82% q10/q12, 18-32% q19 with 7 MB batches). Receiver-side unpack of the same frames: 0.14 ms per 303 MB (2.1 TB/s), ~30x faster than the pack.

**Source (verified).** `compute_node_service.rs:1207-1219` comment: "one FIFO request channel into ONE transport thread ... the drains still run one at a time, in the FE's destination order"; `:380-392 dispatch_worker` is one thread; `:864-872 run_ready_fragment ... .and_then(FragmentOutcome::join_into_ready)` joins the drains before yielding; `nixl_transport.rs:713-775` drain loop (`export_packed_next` per batch, lease RPC, `write_and_wait`, transmit RPC); `engine.rs:813 export_packed_next = engine_call` served by the single engine thread (engine.rs:321-324); `src/sirius_ffi.cpp:~800 kPackChunkBytes = 8 MiB` with `cudf::chunked_pack` on the default stream (~37 `next()` launches per 311 MB batch). The serialisation on the dispatch worker exists because `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1` was set (capture-cn.sh:12; default off); with the default, the same drain holds the RPC open and delays the FE's next deploy stage instead (`Deployer.java:236-243, 318`). Either way it is on the critical path.

**Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). The impact sentence "small fragments could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is wrong for the current engine (one fragment at a time, B1); only the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span, is recoverable.

**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run bench-kit TPC-H queries against the FE on 9030 with a /* marker */ so the FE audit log ties QueryId to (query, run).
# usage: run-queries.sh <tag> <tpch_data> <out_dir> <timeout_s> <runs_after_warmup> q01 q02 ...
# writes <out_dir>/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc) and <out_dir>/<q>.r<i>.out (mysql --batch)
TAG=$1; DATA=$2; OUT=$3; TO=$4; RUNS=$5; shift 5
QD=/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf/experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries
mkdir -p $OUT; echo "query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc" > $OUT/runs.csv
M="mysql --host 127.0.0.1 --port 9030 --user root --batch --connect-timeout=5"
for q in "$@"; do
  sql=$(sed "s#__TPCH_DATA__#$DATA#g" $QD/$q.sql)
  for i in $(seq 0 $RUNS); do
    phase=warm; [ $i = 0 ] && phase=cold
    start=$(date -u +%FT%T.%3N); t0=$(date +%s%N)
    if timeout $TO $M -e "/* $TAG $q r$i */ $sql" > $OUT/$q.r$i.out 2> $OUT/$q.r$i.err; then st=pass; else st=fail; rc=$?; fi
    ms=$(( ($(date +%s%N) - t0) / 1000000 )); rows=$(( $(wc -l < $OUT/$q.r$i.out) - 1 )); [ $rows -lt 0 ] && rows=0
    [ $st = fail ] && [ $ms -ge $((TO*1000 - 500)) ] && st=timeout
    echo "$q,$i,$phase,$st,$ms,$rows,$start" >> $OUT/runs.csv
    echo "$q r$i $phase $st ${ms}ms rows=$rows $( [ $st != pass ] && head -c 160 $OUT/$q.r$i.err | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [ $st != pass ] && break   # a failing run skips the rest of that query (bench.sh semantics)
  done
done
